nodes.name: Fetch Open Leads
nodes.notes: Excludes DISQUALIFIED as well as LOST. A lead row is what makes the WhatsApp bot answer someone unconditionally, so a wrong number written into `leads` by mistake is quarantined with status DISQUALIFIED rather than deleted -- and a quarantined lead must not be chased for silence either. Two were quarantined on 28 Aug: a solar-clamp supplier and a web-design contact, both auto-created when an uncaptioned image tripped the 'document' keyword.

nodes.name: Fetch WhatsApp Contacts
nodes.notes: Added 30 Aug 2026 for the WhatsApp identity fix. A LID chat id (e.g. 158510264357112@lid) carries no phone digits, so it cannot be derived from a lead row. whatsapp_contacts is the chat_id -> phone / lead_email map the WhatsApp BDC workflow already upserts, and is what lets Find Silent Leads reach comms filed under a LID. Non-fatal: if the table is unreachable the detector still matches every non-LID key.

nodes.name: Escalation Landed?
nodes.notes: The sub-workflow reports failure in its payload, not as an error: {status:'escalation_failed', escalated:false}. Only the true branch may write the [SILENCE-ESCALATED] marker; the false branch still reports and audits, and the lead stays in the safety net for the next run.
